decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line with several models close to the core range carries tooling and catalogue investment, and handles typically stay in the range for many years, so dropping it after one year is unlikely.
A multi-model handle family close to the established offer represents meaningful sunk investment, and early results can still be attributed to normal market ramp-up.
A single handle design has less investment and no public commitment, so it is somewhat easier to drop, but one year is too short to judge it a failure.
Like C, it is a single design with limited sunk cost, but within one year a close-to-core handle would normally be kept while sales develop.
A product line with several models builds on the firm's established competence, and its investment and catalogue presence favor persistence.
The L700 electronic access system was publicly launched as a flagship and is central to the firm's announced digital building direction, so management will strongly persist with it.
